Total splenectomy proved hydatid cyst pathologically (E1 confirmatory). Treated with albendazole. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The lesion was proved to be hydatic cyst pathologically.
It had well-defined borders and contained multiple, round, daughter cysts in the periphery of the lesion (Figure 2).
evidence_items.target_concept: Hydatid cyst with peripheral daughter cysts (CE2)

rationale: A 48-year-old male presented with epigastric pain and fever. Abdominal ultrasound showed a septated cystic lesion with honeycomb-like structures in the left hepatic lobe (E2 highly specific). Indirect hemagglutination was positive for echinococcal antibodies. Radical cysto-pericystectomy was performed, and histopathological examination confirmed Echinococcosis (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of Echinococcosis.
Patient underwent ultrasonography of the abdomen that revealed a septated cystic lesion with "honeycomb-like" structures localized in the hepatic left lobe (Figure 1).

rationale: A 72-year-old male presented with acute abdominal pain and distension. Abdominal CT showed a 14.5 cm hepatic hydatid cyst with daughter cysts (CE2) and multiple splenic hydatid cysts. Laparotomy confirmed abdominal and splenic hydatidosis; deroofing, omentoplasty, and splenectomy were performed (E1/E2). Treated with albendazole. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Intraoperative findings confirmed the diagnosis of abdominal and splenic hydatidosis.
evidence_items.test_name: Surgical exploration and macroscopic operative confirmation

evidence_items.source_quote: The CT revealed a huge hepatic hydatid cyst (measuring 14.5 cm) with daughter cysts in the left lobe of the liver and multiple splenic hydatidosis.
evidence_items.target_concept: Hepatic hydatid cyst with daughter cysts (CE2) and splenic hydatidosis

rationale: A 62-year-old male presented with throbbing spinal pain. Thoracic CT revealed multiple thoracic vertebral osteolytic lesions and soft tissue cyst extensions characteristic of diffuse vertebral hydatidosis, and hydatid serology was positive (E2 highly specific). The patient was treated with oral albendazole for two years with documented symptomatic and radiological improvement. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Hydatic serology was positive.
Multiple thoracic vertebral corporeal osteolysis and T8-T10 vertebral block in relation to diffuse vertebral hydatidosis involving thoracic vertebrae with extension to adjacent soft tissues.
evidence_items.target_concept: Diffuse vertebral hydatidosis with soft tissue extension

rationale: A 22-year-old male presented with hemoptysis. Chest radiograph showed a pathognomonic water-lily sign (E2 highly specific) and CT showed multiple cysts in both lungs and spleen. Thoracotomy and cystectomy were performed and hydatid membranes were delivered (E1 confirmatory). Treated with albendazole. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The chest radiograph showed a well circumscribed dense homogeneous opacity in the mid to lower zones of the right hemithorax and a small left lower zone cavity with a water-lily sign and obliteration of the left hemi-diaphragm (Fig. 1).
The operation revealed a large hydatid cyst that ruptured upon efforts to enucleate it. The membranes were delivered

rationale: A 7-year-old girl presented with generalized seizures and hemiparesis. Brain MRI showed a parenchymal spherical cyst with peripheral daughter cysts (E2). Craniotomy was performed and the cyst was delivered intact using the Dowling technique; histopathological examination confirmed hydatid cyst (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of hydatid cyst.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of excised cerebral cyst

evidence_items.source_quote: The walls of the cyst were hypointense on T1- and T2-weighted images (Figure 1) and contain few peripheral daughter cysts.
evidence_items.target_concept: Cerebral hydatid cyst with peripheral daughter cysts (CE2)

rationale: A 9-year-old boy from a rural area presented with a painless limp. Pelvic MRI revealed a Gharbi type II psoas hydatid cyst containing a central floating membrane (E2 highly specific water-lily sign). Surgical intervention was performed via pararectal retroperitoneal approach, suctioning purulent cyst fluid and extracting the proliferous germinal membrane with pericystectomy (E1 confirmatory). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: extraction of the proliferous membrane with realization of a pericystectomy and abundant washing of the residual cavity with physiological saline.
evidence_items.test_name: Surgical pericystectomy and proliferous membrane extraction

evidence_items.source_quote: On MRI, it was a type II psoas hydatid cyst according to GHARBI classification, which appeared in hyposignal in T1 and T2 containing a central floating membrane.
evidence_items.target_concept: Gharbi type II hydatid cyst with central floating membrane (water-lily sign)

rationale: A 15-year-old girl presented with right lumbar pain and hydatiduria. Abdominal ultrasound showed a multiloculated cystic renal lesion with pathognomonic spoke-wheel appearance (CE2) and ELISA for echinococcus antibodies was positive (E2). Right nephroureterectomy was performed, and histopathological examination was consistent with hydatid disease (E1 confirmatory). Treated with albendazole. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathological examination was consistent with hydatid disease.

Ultrasonography of abdomen was suggestive of multiloculated cystic lesion, with typical spoke-wheel appearance, in the mid pole of right kidney and ELISA test was positive for echinococcus antibodies.
evidence_items.target_concept: Typical spoke-wheel appearance (CE2) and echinococcus antibodies

rationale: A 26-year-old male with a history of pet dog contact presented with left hypochondrial pain and an immobile lump. Ultrasound and CT showed an 11 x 8 cm complex cystic lesion arising from the left kidney. Under general anesthesia, laparoscopic transperitoneal deroofing with hypertonic saline protection and evacuation of cyst contents was performed, with meticulous inspection of the cavity for daughter cysts followed by omentoplasty. Patient was pretreated and managed with albendazole. Verified active renal hydatidosis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cyst was then deroofed and contents were evacuated through a 10mm suction port in the left lumbar region. Precaution was taken to minimize the spillage. Cyst cavity was inspected at last for any residual daughter cyst and finally omentoplasty was done (Figure 3).
evidence_items.test_name: Laparoscopic cyst deroofing, evacuation of hydatid contents, and inspection for daughter cysts

evidence_items.source_quote: Ultrasound abdomen done there showed a well-outlined complex cystic lesion, measuring 11 x 8cm containing echogenic fluid collection and arising from infero-medial aspect of left kidney. Computerized tomography (CT) scan reported similar findings (Figure 1).

rationale: A 44-year-old woman presented with persistent neck and back pain and vertebral destruction, initially misdiagnosed and empirically treated as spinal tuberculosis. Effusion fluid mNGS demonstrated 3,938 reads (99.74% of microbial reads) mapping to Echinococcus multilocularis, definitively confirmed by pathogen-specific COX1 gene PCR and Sanger sequencing. Antituberculosis therapy was stopped and albendazole initiated. Confirmed vertebral alveolar echinococcosis (E1 confirmatory) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Therefore, we adopted mNGS to further screen for potential pathogens in this case, and the results revealed high reads count and coverage rate for Echinococcus multilocularis, which was further verified by PCR and Sanger sequencing.

According to the mNGS result, we designed a pair of PCR primers (EfF: 5'-GATTCCTTCTTTAGTTTTGTTGTTGATTAG-3' and EfR: 5'-CGAACTAAAAACTCTAGAAACACCTGCT-3') to specifically amplify the COX1 gene of Echinococcus multilocularis (GenBankTM accession number: AB813188). The sequencing results are consistent with the sequence alignment of the tapeworm cox1 gene, which further confirmed the mNGS results (Figure 4).

rationale: A 13-year-old female presented with right flank pain and a palpable lumbar lump. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a 11.5 x 10.5 x 15.5 cm multiloculated cyst with internal septations and typical 'cysts within cyst' appearance arising from the upper pole of an incomplete duplex kidney (E2). Serum ELISA for Echinococcus antibodies was positive (E2). Simple nephrectomy revealed the upper moiety turned into a bag of cysts, and histopathological examination confirmed hydatid disease of the kidney (E1 confirmatory) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathological examination of the cyst was consistent with the diagnosis of hydatid disease of kidney.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of excised renal cyst

evidence_items.source_quote: Contrast Enhanced Computed Tomography (CECT) showed a large multiloculated cyst of size 11.5cms x 10.5cms x 15.5cms with internal septations arising from the upper pole of right kidney, with typical cysts within cyst appearance and thinned out peripheral parenchyma.
evidence_items.target_concept: Cysts within cyst / multiloculated hydatid cyst (CE2)

evidence_items.source_quote: ELISA test for echinococcus antibodies was positive.

rationale: A 35-year-old female presented with a painless cystic swelling over the right upper chest. CT showed a multiseptated hypodense cystic lesion in the right pectoralis major muscle. Surgical exploration revealed a 6 x 7 cm hydatid cyst containing multiple pathognomonic daughter cysts (E2 highly specific). Verified active musculoskeletal hydatidosis -> POSITIVE.
step4_condition_matched: Hydatid cyst with daughter cysts / Echinococcosis

evidence_items.source_quote: Per-op finding revealed a 6 x 7 cm hydatid cyst in the right pectoralis major muscle with multiple daughter cysts (Fig. 4, Fig. 5, Fig. 6).
evidence_items.target_concept: Hydatid cyst with multiple daughter cysts

evidence_items.source_quote: On further work up, a computed tomography scan of the chest demonstrated a multiseptated hypodense cystic lesion in the right pectoralis major muscle with no intralesional calcification and no intrathoracic extension (Figs. 1-3).

rationale: An 86-year-old female presenting with chronic cough, dyspnea, and a history of hepatic hydatid cyst. Thoracic CT and MRI confirmed multiseptated cystic filling defects within the right main pulmonary trunk and right lower lobe, bilateral parenchymal hydatid cysts, and a large hepatic hydatid cyst. Follow-up after dual antiparasitic therapy (albendazole and praziquantel) showed regression of the pulmonary artery and parenchymal cysts. Verified active pulmonary artery and multiorgan hydatid disease (E2 highly specific) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: We conducted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the thorax, which confirmed the presence of the cystic lesion within the right pulmonary trunk extending to the right lower lobe, showing low signal intensity on T1 and high intensity on T2 images with septation (see Figures 4 and 5).
evidence_items.target_concept: Intravascular pulmonary trunk hydatid cyst with septation

evidence_items.source_quote: The CT showed multiple intraluminal cystic filling defects in the right main pulmonary artery and right lobar branches, mostly pulmonary artery hydatid cysts (see Figures 1 and 2).

rationale: A 69-year-old female presenting with dyspepsia and a gastric bulge on endoscopy. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) revealed a 90.8 x 17.2 mm cystic lesion originating in the left liver lobe with a pathognomonic floating membrane inside (WHO CE3 / water-lily sign, E2). Surgical resection and histopathology definitively confirmed a hydatid cyst with characteristic lamellar cuticular membrane pattern and a vestigial protoscolex (E1 confirmatory) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: In the internal surface of the lesion, there were remains of membranous structures amidst, in which a vestigial Protoscolex was noted.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of resected liver cyst

evidence_items.source_quote: The cyst wall revealed a characteristic lamellar pattern of the fibers.

Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) was performed and showed a heterogeneous lesion, mainly anechogenic one, with a floating membrane inside, and greatest diameter of 90.8 x 17.2 mm, originated in the liver left lobe (Figure 2). The diagnosis of a hydatid cyst type 3 was made.
evidence_items.target_concept: Hydatid cyst CE3 with floating membrane (water-lily sign)

rationale: A 28-year-old man presented with exertional dyspnea and a giant right hemithorax cyst (20 x 18 x 14 cm). Right posterolateral thoracotomy was performed, evacuating 2500 cc of fluid and removing the characteristic laminated membrane of the hydatid cyst (E1 confirmatory). Treated postoperatively with oral albendazole with complete clinical resolution. Confirmed pulmonary hydatidosis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient underwent right posterolateral thoracotomy through the 6th intercostal space, in which the cyst contents including 2500 cc clear fluid and the laminated membrane of the hydatid cyst were removed.
evidence_items.test_name: Thoracotomy and surgical removal of hydatid cyst contents

rationale: A 38-year-old male presented with dyspnea and was found to have a 90 x 60 mm cystic mass embedded in the left ventricular myocardium. Under left thoracotomy, the myocardial mass was approached, revealing pale yellow daughter cysts; scolicidal solution was injected and multiple daughter cysts were surgically removed (E2 highly specific). Uneventful recovery. Confirmed cardiac hydatidosis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: After pericardium reflection, the mass with its pale yellow daughter cysts was visible [Figure 5].
Multiple daughter cysts were removed [Figure 6].
evidence_items.test_name: Intraoperative surgical evacuation of daughter cysts

rationale: A 35-year-old female from rural background presented with pain and swelling over the right TMJ and ramus condyle unit of the mandible. CT showed a 4.9 x 3.8 cm encapsulated cystic lesion causing osteolysis. Surgical excision was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated daughter cysts with scolex and germinal layers (E1 confirmatory). Confirmed mandibular hydatidosis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: In histopathology, scanner view, x10 view and x 40 view showing daughter cysts with scolex and germinal layers [Figures 5-7].
evidence_items.target_concept: Daughter cysts with scolex and germinal layers

rationale: A 62-year-old male farmer presented with a 12-year history of painful gluteal mass and hip restriction. Hydatid serology (RIDASCREEN Echinococcus IgG ELISA) was strongly positive above cutoff (E2). CT and MRI revealed a multiloculated pelvic cyst with bone destruction. The patient received albendazole and underwent en bloc surgical excision; histopathology demonstrated daughter cysts and lamellated cuticular membranes (E1 confirmatory) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Hydatid serology using immunoglobulin G (IgG) enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) (RIDASCREEN Echinococcus IgG, R-Biopharm AG, Germany) was performed following the manufacturer's instruction, and surprisingly, the optical density value was above the cutoff.

Hematoxylin and eosin stainingrevealed a thick cyst wall with few daughter cysts, occasional calcified foci with intense inflammatory responses, and exuberant giant cell reaction against lamellated membranes [Figures 2 and 3] consistent with hydatid cyst.

rationale: A 16-year-old female presented with generalized tonic-clonic seizures and headache. Contrast-enhanced brain MRI showed a 5 x 4.9 x 4.8 cm cystic lesion in the left fronto-temporal region with multiple daughter cysts within a large cyst (E2). Fronto-temporal craniotomy was performed, and histopathological examination confirmed a hydatid cyst (E1 confirmatory). Treated with albendazole. Verified cerebral hydatid disease -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The sample was sent for histopathological examination, which confirmed it as a hydatid cyst.

MRI of brain with contrast showed well-defined peripherally enhancing rounded predominantly cystic lesion of size 5 x 4.9 x 4.8 cm in left fronto-temporal region with multiple daughter cysts within a large cyst suggestive of intra-cerebral hydatid cyst.
evidence_items.target_concept: Cystic lesion with multiple daughter cysts (CE2)

rationale: A 52-year-old male shepherd presented with abdominal pain, cough, and jaundice. CT showed multiloculated cystic lesions with septations in the right lung, liver, and spleen. Thoracotomy and laparotomy were performed, successfully extracting the pulmonary hydatid cyst, extracting all daughter cysts from the liver, and marsupializing the splenic cysts. Histopathology confirmed hydatid cyst of the liver and spleen (E1 confirmatory). Managed with albendazole. Verified multiorgan hydatid disease -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The samples were sent for histopathology, and the report confirmed a hydatid cyst of the liver and spleen.
evidence_items.target_concept: Hydatid cyst of liver and spleen

evidence_items.source_quote: All daughter cysts were extracted with due precautions, with no spillage in the peritoneal cavity.
The computed tomography (CT) report was suggestive of a hydatid cyst in the right lung (Figure 1).

rationale: A 30-year-old female presented with left lumbar dull pain. Abdominal ultrasonography demonstrated an 11.6 x 5.5 cm multivesicular formation with characteristic 'honeycomb like' appearance (pathognomonic WHO CE2 / type III hydatid cyst, E2). CT showed thick septations, and left total nephrectomy confirmed a grape-shaped multivesicular cystic tumor intraoperatively (E2). Successfully managed with albendazole and surgery without recurrence at 1 year -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote:
A multivesicular formation was discovered by abdominal ultrasonography involving the upper pole of the left kidney and measuring 11.6 cm x 5.5 cm. This formation had the characteristic "honeycomb like" appearance. There is no evidence of solid components.
A hydatid cyst type III was evoked (Figure 1).
evidence_items.target_concept: Multivesicular honeycomb cyst (WHO CE2 / Type III)

evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnosis was confirmed intraoperatively by macroscopic data: A cystic tumor shaped like a grape.

rationale: A 4-year-old male child with contact history with cattle and dogs presented with gait instability, weakness, and fever. Brain MRI revealed a 13-cm cystic lesion in the left parietooccipital region. The giant cyst was enucleated successfully without rupture, and histopathological examination definitively confirmed a hydatid cyst (E1 confirmatory). Treated with albendazole with complete recovery -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathological examination was reported as compatible with a hydatid cyst.

The magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) then revealed a 13 cm-in-diameter cystic lesion surrounded by vasogenic edema in the left parietooccipital region (Fig. 1). The cystic lesion was consistent with a 'hydatid cyst' because of the absence of a solid component.

rationale: A 30-year-old female presenting with chronic cough and hemoptysis. CT demonstrated bilateral pulmonary cystic lesions and a hepatic cyst, with the right lung lesion exhibiting the pathognomonic 'water lily sign' (WHO CE3a, E2). Bilateral thoracotomies and liver resection were performed; pathology demonstrated protoscolices and refractile hooks of Echinococcus confirmed with Grocott and PAS stains (E1 confirmatory). Treated with albendazole. Confirmed cystic echinococcosis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathology studies revealed the presence of cystic echinococcosis in both lungs and liver, with evidence of protoscolices and refractory hooks of echinococcal scolex, highlighted by the Grocott technique; Ziehl-Neelsen and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) were found (Figure 4(a) and (b)).
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathology with Grocott, PAS, and ZN stains

evidence_items.source_quote: A computed tomography (CT) showed the presence of round cystic lesions, with defined contours in the lower pulmonary lobes and a cystic image in the liver; one image in the right lung was compatible with "the water lily sign" (Figure 1(b) and (c)).

rationale: A 34-year-old female presented with back pain and fever. Chest CT revealed a cystic lesion in the right lower pulmonary lobe, and immunological serology was positive for echinococcosis (E2). Right thoracotomy and cyst resection was performed, with pathological examination confirming the presence of echinococcal scolex and hooks (E1 confirmatory) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathological studies reported the presence of hooks in the right lung lesion, with the presence of echinococcal scolex (Figure 8).
Suspecting echinococcosis immunological test were done and these were positive for echinococcosis.

rationale: A 15-year-old male with dog contact presented with cough, hydatidoptysis, chest pain, and hydropneumothorax due to cyst rupture. Hydatid serology was strongly positive at 6.6 (E2). Right posterolateral thoracotomy revealed and extracted a pleural hydatid cyst in its entirety with decortication and albendazole medical therapy (E2). Good clinical and radiological recovery -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Hydatid serology was positive at 6.6.

A posterolateral right thoracotomy was performed, revealing a healthy hydatid cyst at the pleural level with fibrin deposits. The cyst was extracted in its entirety, and the fibrin deposits were removed.

rationale: A 12-year-old boy presenting to the emergency department with acute chest pain, dyspnea, cyanosis, and fainting due to tension pneumothorax secondary to a ruptured hydatid cyst. Emergency left thoracotomy, cystotomy, and capitonnage directly identified, confirmed, and evacuated a large ruptured hydatid cyst in the upper lobe of the left lung (E2 highly specific). Successfully treated surgically with antiparasitic coverage -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The surgeons performed left thoracotomy, cystotomy, and capitonnage of a large ruptured hydatid cyst in the upper lobe of the left lung.

Unlike other causes, tension pneumothorax due to a pulmonary hydatid cyst requires surgical and antiparasitic treatment to prevent recurrence, unlike other causes. In such cases, tension pneumothorax should be controlled, and hydatid cysts should be treated surgically as soon as possible.

rationale: A 36-year-old male presented with an 11 x 7 cm cystic lesion in the right superior lung lobe and a splenic cyst. Specific serology for Echinococcus granulosus was positive (E2). Follow-up chest CT demonstrated thick-walled cyst with fluid content and wavy lines inside the cavity (floating endocyst membrane / water-lily sign, CE3a, E2). Surgical pericystectomy with hypertonic saline protection and albendazole therapy was performed, with complete recovery -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: serology for E. granulosustested positive.

ABZ was started once again, and a new CT scan of the chest showed a change in the appearance of the lung cyst, which was now surrounded by a thick wall with fluid content and wavy lines inside the cavity.
evidence_items.target_concept: Floating membranes / wavy lines inside cavity (CE3a / water-lily sign)

rationale: A 36-year-old male from Kashmir presented with jaundice and right upper quadrant abdominal mass. Abdominal CECT revealed a large (12.5 cm) solid-cystic intrahepatic lesion with peripheral subtle curvilinear and central nodular calcification, suspicious for malignancy. Liver biopsy definitively demonstrated foci of eosinophilic necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes with pale refractile, strongly PAS-positive laminated membranes classical for alveolar echinococcosis (E1 confirmatory). Confirmed hepatic alveolar echinococcosis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The liver biopsy highlighted multiple randomly dispersed foci of eosinophilic necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes, a pale zone of fibrosis, and a thick collar of lymphocytes at places (Figures 2A and 2B). These foci of necrosis were dominantly lobular, at places confluent, giving rise to large necrotic areas. A few foci contained pale, refractile eosinophilic membranes, which were strongly PAS-positive (Figures 2C and 2D). No tumor was seen. This morphology was classical to alveolar echinococcosis.
evidence_items.test_name: Liver biopsy histopathology and PAS stain

evidence_items.source_quote:
The abdominal contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) revealed a large solid-cystic intrahepatic lesion measuring 125x118x123 mm involving the hepatic segments IV, VII, and VIII (Figure 1). 
This lesion showed peripheral subtle curvilinear and central nodular calcification.

rationale: A 37-year-old male farmer presenting with left shoulder pain and a cystic mass in the infraspinatus muscle. Echinococcal indirect hemagglutination (IHA) was positive. The mass was excised en bloc, and histopathology confirmed Echinococcosis by demonstrating protoscolices and germinative membrane infecting muscle tissue (E1 confirmatory evidence) -> POSITIVE.
step4_condition_matched: Echinococcosis / Hydatid cyst of infraspinatus muscle

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathology preparations showed chronic inflammatory tissue along with protoscolices infecting muscle tissue and germinative membrane (Fig. 3).
Serological evaluation with echinococcal indirect hemagglutination (IHA) test yielded positive results.

rationale: A 15-year-old female presenting with suprapubic discomfort and constipation, found to have a pelvic cystic mass in the Pouch of Douglas with internal membranes and cyst-within-a-cyst appearance. Echinococcus IgG antibodies were positive. Complete surgical excision was performed, and microscopy definitively confirmed Echinococcosis by identifying hooklets, protoscolices, and daughter cysts (E1 confirmatory evidence) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Microscopy showed hooklets, protoscolices, and daughter cysts strongly suggestive of Echinococcus. The diagnosis was confirmed by histopathology.
evidence_items.target_concept: Echinococcus hooklets, protoscolices, and daughter cysts

evidence_items.source_quote: Internal enhancing membranes with cyst within the cyst appearance was seen [Figure 1b].
evidence_items.target_concept: Internal enhancing membranes with cyst-within-a-cyst appearance (WHO CE2)

rationale: A 26-year-old female who underwent a PAIR procedure for a type 1 hepatic hydatid cyst using ethanol, acutely developing sclerosing cholangitis and liver failure requiring emergency living donor liver transplantation. Histopathological examination of the explanted liver confirmed a segmental hydatid cyst partially ruptured into the major bile ducts (E1 confirmatory evidence) -> POSITIVE.
step4_condition_matched: Type 1 hydatid cyst / Hepatic hydatid disease

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathological examination of the explanted liver revealed a segmental hydatid cyst that had partially ruptured into the major bile ducts, with mucosal ulceration observed in the extrahepatic biliary tract and increased connective tissue thickening of the duct.
evidence_items.target_concept: Segmental hydatid cyst ruptured into major bile ducts

evidence_items.source_quote: A 26-year-old female patient underwent a PAIR procedure at another medical center for the management of a type 1 hydatid cyst located in segment 7 of the liver, using ethanol as the scolicidal agent.
evidence_items.target_concept: Type 1 hydatid cyst of liver (WHO CE1)

rationale: A 60-year-old female sheep herder from Eritrea presenting with progressive unilateral proptosis and vision loss, found to have an orbital cystic mass. Anterior orbitotomy with surgical excision was performed, and biopsy confirmed a hydatid cyst by demonstrating an acellular laminated membrane, germinal epithelium, and a daughter cyst with protoscolices (E1 confirmatory evidence) -> POSITIVE.
step4_condition_matched: Hydatid cyst of the orbit / Echinococcosis

evidence_items.source_quote: Biopsy result revealed an acellular laminated membrane with germinal epithelium and a daughter cyst with protoscolices (Figure 2A and B) and surrounding soft tissue consisting of chronic inflammatory cells confirming the diagnosis of hydatid cyst.
evidence_items.target_concept: Acellular laminated membrane, germinal epithelium, and daughter cyst with protoscolices

rationale: A 57-year-old male presenting with progressive dyspnea and a massive recurrent thoracoabdominal hydatid cyst measuring 16x9 cm, classified as Gharbi Type 2-3 with extraparenchymal extensions containing membranous structures on CT. Surgical excision was performed with extraction of germinative membrane fragments from the capsule (E2 pathognomonic imaging and surgical membrane extraction) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The thoracoabdominal CT scan disclosed calcific alterations in the surrounding tissue, along with a hydatid cyst classified as Type 2-3 according to the Gharbi classification. This cyst exhibited a slight wall calcification, spanning approximately 16 x 9 cm, encompassing the entirety of the right hepatic lobe, with extraparenchymal extensions containing membranous structures.
evidence_items.target_concept: Gharbi Type 2-3 hydatid cyst with membranous structures

evidence_items.source_quote: efforts were made to extract tissue fragments suggestive of germinative membrane from the capsule.
evidence_items.test_name: Surgical exploration and cyst wall excision
evidence_items.target_concept: Germinative membrane fragments extracted from capsule

step10_contradiction_notes: Echinococcal IHA titer at 1/80 was negative, but active recurrent disease was definitively confirmed by pathognomonic Gharbi 2-3 imaging and surgical extraction of germinative membrane.

rationale: A 20-year-old postpartum woman presenting with acute peritonitis secondary to a ruptured hepatic hydatid cyst. Abdominal CT showed a collapsed cystic lesion with pathognomonic serpentine floating structures and spillage of contents into the peritoneal cavity (E2 pathognomonic imaging). Emergency laparotomy confirmed a ruptured hydatid cyst with peritoneal spillage and partial cystectomy was successfully performed -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was performed, revealing a peripheral superficial collapsed cystic lesion in the left lobe (II segment) of the liver that has lost its spherical shape, with thick enhancing walls and a parietal defect, consistent with a ruptured hydatid cyst. Evidence of spillage of cyst contents into the peritoneal cavity appearing as serpentine structures, were noted, along with diffuse thickened peritoneal enhancement and free peritoneal fluid (Figure 1).
evidence_items.target_concept: Collapsed cyst with serpentine floating structures and peritoneal spillage

evidence_items.source_quote: Intraoperatively, a large ruptured cyst was found on the inferior side of the II segment of the liver, with spillage of hydatid cyst contents into the peritoneal cavity associated to a yellow serous fluid (Figure 2).
evidence_items.target_concept: Ruptured hydatid cyst with contents spilled into peritoneal cavity

rationale: A 66-year-old female presenting with a 3-year history of painless swelling in the left neck and supraclavicular area. Surgical exploration revealed cystic lesions from which cyst fluid was aspirated, characteristic cyst membranes were removed, and the cyst wall was resected. Histopathologic examination confirmed the diagnosis of hydatid cyst for both lesions (E1 confirmatory evidence) -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Approximately 8 cm lesion was incised, clear yellow-colored cyst fluid was aspirated, cyst membranes were located and removed, and cyst wall was resected.
evidence_items.target_concept: Cyst membranes removed and cyst wall resected

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathologic diagnosis was reported as hydatid cyst for both lesions.

rationale: A 44-year-old female presenting with frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), found on TTE/TEE/MRI to have an oscillating cystic mass attached to the right ventricular papillary muscle via chordae tendineae. Echinococcal IgG ELISA was positive (E2 strong evidence), and targeted albendazole therapy resulted in documented complete resolution of the intracardiac mass and symptom remission -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: With a suspicion of hydatid cyst, echinococcal IgG enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was done and was positive.
A second follow-up a month later showed complete resolution of the mass and a decline in PVCs (Panels G and H) with a 24-h PVC burden of 6%, confirming the diagnosis of cardiac hydatid cyst.
evidence_items.target_concept: Complete resolution of intracardiac cystic mass confirming cardiac hydatid cyst

rationale: A 43-year-old female presenting with cough, fever, salty taste in saliva, and breathlessness. Thoracic CT showed multiple rounded cystic lesions in the right lower lobe with air-fluid level and loculated hydropneumothorax.
